source.title: More evidence for a relational shift in the development of analogy: Children's performance on a causal-mapping task

confidence_rationale: Supports the reality of relational (structure-based) mapping as a distinct mode that children come to prefer over object-similarity mapping, which is the phenomenon MECH-421 names. Mixed for the build-vs-emerge question: the shift is attributed to growth of relational domain knowledge rather than maturation of a new mapping mechanism, which favours emergence from richer relational representations while presupposing a mapping process present throughout. Verified only via search-engine records (ScienceDirect, APA PsycNet, Northwestern author PDF header); full text not read in this session, so confidence is held down.
failure_signatures: The finding is a preference shift in which match children choose; it does not show whether the mapping process itself is innate or learned, so it can be over-read in either direction.
Contested by Goswami's evidence that young children solve familiar causal analogies; the shift may reflect task familiarity and knowledge rather than any change in analogy machinery.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Children first interpret analogies in terms of object similarity and later in terms of relational similarity (the relational shift); a causal-mapping task gives further evidence for this shift, which Gentner attributes to accruing relational knowledge.
mapping.ree_translation: Developmental evidence that surface-feature matching is the default and relational mapping is what the agent grows into as its relational representations deepen. For Q-074 this fits the 'emerges from the relational stack' horn: analogy quality tracks the richness of MECH-419/MECH-420 representations rather than the arrival of a new operator.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Structure-mapping theory still assumes one alignment process throughout development; the knowledge-driven shift does not show that alignment itself emerges. Both Q-074 horns can accommodate this result, so its discriminating power is low.
mapping.source_context: Behavioral experiments with preschool and school-age children on a causal-mapping analogy task, framed as a reply to Goswami (1996).

confidence_components.notes: Classic peer-reviewed developmental study; metadata verified via search records only (publisher pages blocked by proxy), abstract-level reading.
